L102: ## Build on Learning From Work, Service, and Experience
L103: 
L104: Learning does not only happen in a college classroom. You may have gained college-level knowledge through military service, professional training, certifications, exams, or other structured learning experiences. UMass Global offers several ways to review eligible prior learning. The option that fits you depends on the learning you completed and the program you want to pursue.
L105: ### ACE-Recommended Learning
L106: 
L107: Have training, military learning, exams, or approved alternative coursework? ACE recommendations may help you identify credit that may be reviewed.
L108: 
L109: 【51†Explore ACE Learning】
L110: 
L111: ### Program-Specific Credit Opportunities
L112: 
L113: Some programs recognize eligible certifications, credentials, training, and prior learning for course credit or substitutions.
L114: 
L115: 【52†Find Programs】
L116: ## ACE-Recommended Learning
L117: 
L118: The American Council on Education, or ACE, reviews certain learning completed outside a traditional college classroom. UMass Global accepts eligible ACE credit recommendations, subject to program requirements and other academic policies. ACE may include recommendations for:
L119: 
L120:   * Military courses, training, and occupations
L121:   * Employer and workforce training
L122:   * Professional and technical learning
L123:   * Approved alternative courses
L124:   * Some examinations
L125: Use the ACE National Guide to search for your course, training, credential, or exam. Then apply to UMass Global and submit documentation for review.
L126: 
L127: 【53†Search the ACE National Guide†www.acenet.edu】
L128: 
L129: ACE recommendations can help you understand what may be reviewed. UMass Global determines how eligible credit applies toward your selected degree.
L130: 
L131: * * *
L132: 
L133: 【54†Image】
L134: ## Continue Your Education With Sophia or Study.com
L135: 
L136: Have you completed courses through Sophia or Study.com? Eligible coursework may help you make progress toward a UMass Global degree. Eligible students may also receive a 10-20% tuition discount, depending on their program.
L137: 
L138: 【55†Explore Sophia Partnership】
L139: 
L140: 
L141: 
L142: 【56†Explore Study.com Partnership】
L143: ## Credit by Exam
L144: 
L145: You may be able to earn credit for knowledge you have already demonstrated. UMass Global accepts eligible scores from:
L146: 
L147:   * Advanced Placement (AP)
L148:   * College Level Examination Program (CLEP)
L149:   * DANTES Subject Standardized Tests (DSST)
L150:   * International Baccalaureate (IB)
L151:   * Defense Language Proficiency Examinations (DLAT/DLPT)
L152:   * Subject matter specific exams from institutionally accredited providers
L153:   * Selected UMass Global credit-by-exam opportunities
L154: Credit depends on the exam, your score, and current UMass Global requirements. In some cases, eligible credit may meet general education, major, or elective requirements. Credits are typically lower division unless specified as equivalent to an upper division course.
L155: 
L156: 【57†View Details†catalog.umassglobal.edu】
L157: ## Credit for Military Training and Experience
L158: 
L159: Your military service, coursework, training, and experience may help you make progress toward a UMass Global degree. For undergraduate programs, UMass Global reviews military learning using ACE credit evaluation guidelines.
L160: 
L161: Undergraduate military students receive 6 credits for military service. Additional credit may be awarded based on ACE recommendations.
L162: For graduate programs, military coursework may be considered by programs that accept it. Requirements vary by program.
L163: 
L164: What you may need:
L165: 
L166:   * Military education or training records
L167:   * Joint Services Transcript, if applicable
L168:   * Previous college transcripts
L169:   * Your intended UMass Global program
L170: 
L171: 【58†Explore the ACE Military Guide†militaryguide.acenet.edu】
L172: ## See How Your Training or Certification May Shorten Your Program
L173: 
L174: Some UMass Global programs recognize eligible certifications, credentials, training, and professional learning for credit or course substitutions. Choose the option that best matches your experience.
L175: 
L176: Your teaching credential, induction experience, or authorization may help you complete fewer requirements in select UMass Global education programs. Choose the option that matches your experience and career goal.
L177: MA in Bilingual Education: Build on your authorization
L178: 
L179: Complete UMass Global’s CTEL Authorization or any Bilingual Authorization program, and you may have 6 credits satisfied in the Master of Arts in Bilingual Education. 【59†Explore the MA in Bilingual Education】
L180: 
L181: MA in Education: Build on your teaching experience
L182: Eligible students with a valid U.S. state-issued teaching credential or license may receive 12 credits toward the Master of Arts in Education. California teachers who completed a CTC-approved Teacher Induction or PASC Program may also qualify. 【60†Explore the Master of Arts in Education】
L183: 
L184: MA in Teaching: Build on your California credential
L185: A valid California Preliminary or Clear teaching credential may fulfill 30 credits in the matching Master of Arts in Teaching program. Select the program that matches your credential area.
L186:   * Multiple Subject Credential: Complete your remaining 12 credits in the 【61†MAT in Elementary Education】
L187:   * Single Subject Credential: Complete your remaining 12 credits in the 【62†MAT in Secondary Education】
L188:   * Mild to Moderate Support Needs Credential: Continue into the 【63†MAT with MMSN Ed Specialist Credential】
L189: Eligible current or recently recertified HR credentials—including PHR, SPHR, GPHR, SHRM-CP, and SHRM-SCP—may reduce required coursework in the Master of Science in Human Resources. Certification or recertification must be within the past three years. 【64†Explore the MS in Human Resources】
L190: 
L191: Eligible current certifications from providers such as CompTIA, Cisco, Microsoft, CIW, and others may help you complete fewer requirements in a BS in Information Technology program.
L192: BS in Information Technology — Instructor-Led
L193: 
L194: Review current eligible certifications and course-credit details for the instructor-led program. 【65†Explore the Instructor-Led BSIT】

L198: Review current eligible certifications and course-credit details for the self-paced MyPath program. 【66†Explore the Self-Paced BSIT】
L199: Your California Basic POST Certificate may count for 15 lower-division general elective credits toward the Bachelor of Arts in Criminal Justice. These credits count toward your total degree requirements, but not directly toward the Criminal Justice major. 【67†Explore the BA in Criminal Justice】

L231: ## Prior Learning Assessment (PLA) by Portfolio
L232: 
L233: Some undergraduate students may be able to earn credit for learning gained through work, life, or other non-college experiences. Through a portfolio, you can show how your learning meets the objectives of a UMass Global course.
L234: 
L235: Portfolio credit is awarded for demonstrated learning—not for a job title or years of experience. A separate portfolio is required for each 3-credit course, and a maximum of 30 credits may be awarded through portfolio assessment.
L236: For more information, review the 【68†Prior Learning Assessment by Portfolio Policy†catalog.umassglobal.edu】 or speak with an enrollment coach.
L237: 
L238: 【69†Image】
L239: ## Apply and have your prior learning reviewed
L240: 
L241: Apply to UMass Global—it’s free. After you apply, UMass Global will evaluate your transcripts and supporting documents to determine how eligible credit may apply to your degree.
L242: 
L243:   * 【50†Apply Now】
L244:   * Talk to an enrollment coach
L245: 
L246: ## Frequently Asked Questions
L247: #### [Button: What is Credit for Prior Learning? ]
L248: 
L249: Credit for Prior Learning may help you earn credit for learning completed outside a traditional college course. This may include military training, professional certifications, workforce training, qualifying exams, ACE-recommended learning, or a prior learning portfolio.
L250: 
L251: UMass Global reviews your documentation to determine whether credit may apply to your program.
L252: #### [Button: What do I need to submit for a CPL review? ]
L253: 
L254: What you submit depends on the type of learning you want reviewed. You may need transcripts, exam scores, certification records, training documents, military records, or a Joint Services Transcript.
L255: 
L256: Apply to UMass Global and send any available documents. Your enrollment coach can help you understand what to submit.
L257: #### [Button: Is Credit for Prior Learning guaranteed? ]
L258: 
L259: No. Credit depends on your documentation, your program requirements, and current UMass Global policies. Eligible credit may apply to general education, major, or elective requirements, depending on the review.
